description: Brazilian collateralized consumer-lending platform — home-equity and auto-backed loans at lower APRs than unsecured credit. At Series C: a direct attack on Brazil's extortionate consumer-credit spreads by introducing asset-backed underwriting at scale.
current_status: Collateralized lending platform at $4.8B valuation from Jan 2022 Series F ($260M). No new funding rounds since. Navigating high-Selic environment (14.75%) which compresses margins on secured lending. Expanding product lines beyond auto and home equity. Path to profitability remains the central question.

founder.name: Sergio Furio
founder.background: Spanish, ex-Deutsche Bank / BCG. Career specialization in structured and collateralized credit before founding Creditas — moved to Brazil specifically because he saw unsecured-credit spreads were extortionate and nobody was productizing asset-backed lending at scale.
founder.problem_fit: EXCEPTIONAL. Operated in exactly this domain — the thesis didn't require retraining.
founder.execution_evidence: Shipped product across home-equity, auto, and payroll-linked lending; scaled origination to R$1B+ monthly; navigated 2021 reset with a -31% mark vs Kavak's -75%.
founder.red_flags: None on founder fit. The open question is whether a single founder can make the strategic jump from credit-ops operator to a profitable bank CEO.

stage_context.vs_base: Secured-lending unit economics justify surviving (+5pp) but the Brazilian rate cycle caps thriving (-5pp) and breakout (-5pp). Zombie risk elevated (+5pp) because asset-backed books grow linearly with capital — harder to compound at venture velocity than pure software.

verdict: Creditas survives IF (a) collateralized-loan loss ratios stay below 3.5% through the 2022-2026 high-Selic cycle, (b) funding cost compresses faster than portfolio yield (securitization market depth in Brazil), (c) the home-equity origination engine reaches R$2B/month before capital runs out. Most fragile: (b) — Brazilian securitization depth is thin; Creditas still warehouses much of its book.
top_risk: Interest-rate mismatch: originations are long-duration, funding is short-duration, and high Selic has compressed NIM for three years running
top_opportunity: Payroll-loan channel (consignado) via Creditas @ Work has low loss ratios and sticky corporate relationships — a clear margin pocket vs competitors
actual_outcome: Survived the 2021 valuation reset better than feared (down from $4.8B to $3.3B = -31%, vs Kavak -75%). Unit economics now working at the contract level but overall P&L still underwater. This is the textbook 'big but not yet good' fintech — will either turn into a large, profitable bank-lite over the next 3 years or get acquired by an incumbent wanting the origination tech. Unicorn survival likely; 10x exit unlikely.
